instructions: Put the quinoa in a fine strainer and rinse it under cold water for 30 seconds. Shake it dry.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells good.
Add the quinoa and stir for 1 minute. Add 1 3/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt, and bring it to a boil.
Turn the heat to low, cover, and cook for 14 minutes, until the water is gone and the quinoa is tender. Take it off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse and drain the black beans. Thinly slice 4 of the green onions and chop 1/4 cup of the cilantro. Dice the red bell pepper.
In a large bowl, whisk the juice of the 2 limes (that should be about 3 tbsp), the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil, the honey, chili powder, cumin, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the black pepper.
Fluff the quinoa with a fork and spread it on a plate for 5 minutes to cool. Transfer it into the bowl with the dressing.
Add the black beans, corn, bell pepper, green onions and cilantro. Stir gently until everything is coated.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Divide it into 4 containers. It keeps in the fridge for 4 days and is good cold, so there's no need to reheat it.
method_notes: Kristine's Kitchen (4.95, 51 ratings) is the lead: quinoa toasted with garlic and cooked in a measured amount of liquid, then tossed with black beans, corn, red pepper and a honey, chili powder and cumin lime dressing. Meals by Mavis has no ratings and leans on more lime and cherry tomatoes with no honey. This one follows the lead, uses water instead of broth, thaws nothing (frozen corn goes in as is and defrosts in the salad), and leaves out the avocado so it packs for days. Kristine's Kitchen gives 3 to 4 days in the fridge.
